title: Advanced Board Metrics and Investor Narratives
description: Practice crafting compelling board narratives, interpreting complex metrics, and navigating high-stakes investor scenarios.

interactions.prompt: Series B SaaS company: ARR grew 85% YoY to $18M, but net revenue retention dropped from 130% to 108%, and CAC payback extended from 14 to 22 months. What should the board deck headline?

options.text: ARR growth validates product-market fit trajectory
Growth is masking deteriorating unit economics and retention
CAC payback still within acceptable SaaS benchmarks
NRR above 100% proves strong customer satisfaction

interactions.prompt: Your board meeting is in 48 hours. You just discovered Q3 bookings will miss forecast by 30%. Your lead investor is also your board chair. Do you:

options.text: Call the board chair immediately with the miss and remediation plan
Wait until the meeting to present with full context
Send a pre-read memo to all board members tonight
Reframe the deck around leading indicators that are improving

interactions.prompt: In investor communications, the 'Rule of ____' combines revenue growth rate and profit margin, and top-quartile SaaS companies target above 40.

options.text: 3x

interactions.prompt: You're preparing a Series C board deck after a quarter with mixed results. Rank these sections by the order they should appear to maintain credibility and narrative control:

options.text: Detailed financial results versus plan
CEO framing: what happened, why, and what's changing
Forward-looking strategy and updated targets
Key risks and mitigation plans

interactions.prompt: Fundraising deck shows: $42M ARR, 70% gross margin, 18-month runway, 3.2x LTV/CAC, and 95% logo retention. A top-tier VC passes saying 'the economics don't work at scale.' What's the most likely concern?

options.text: Logo retention is strong but revenue retention likely trails
3.2x LTV/CAC is too low for venture-scale returns
70% gross margin suggests services-heavy revenue that won't scale
18-month runway shows poor capital efficiency

interactions.prompt: During a board Q&A, a director asks about a competitor's recent $200M raise. Your VP Sales looks visibly nervous. You haven't prepared a competitive response. Do you:

options.text: Acknowledge the raise and pivot to your differentiated win rates
Minimize the competitor's raise as mostly marketing spend
Promise a full competitive analysis at the next meeting
Ask the board member what specific concerns they have first

interactions.prompt: You're crafting a fundraising narrative for a $50M Series D. Rank these narrative elements by impact on sophisticated growth-equity investors:

options.text: Path to profitability with specific margin expansion levers
TAM expansion thesis with new product-line evidence
Cohort economics showing improving retention over 8 quarters
Founding team pedigree and notable customer logos

interactions.prompt: Your largest customer (12% of ARR) just churned. The board deck you finalized yesterday positioned NRR expansion as the core growth thesis. With the meeting tomorrow morning, what's your move?

options.text: Rewrite the deck overnight to center on new-logo acquisition engine
Keep the deck but open with the churn, updated NRR, and concentration risk plan
Present the original deck and disclose the churn in Q&A if asked
Email the board tonight requesting to postpone one week

interactions.priorContext: You had finalized a board deck positioning net revenue retention as the company's primary growth engine. Overnight, your largest customer representing 12% of ARR notified they are churning, fundamentally undermining the deck's core thesis.
